amendments.title: Added Ninth Schedule protecting land reform laws from judicial review, added reasonable restrictions on speech, saving of estate acquisition laws
Readjusted Lok Sabha representation scale, allowing one member to represent over 7,50,000 persons
Empowered Parliament to control production, supply and distribution of foodstuffs and raw materials in public interest
Placed compensation for compulsory property acquisition beyond court scrutiny, authorised state to nationalise trade
Empowered President to fix time-limit for state legislatures to express views on Central legislation affecting state boundaries
Added inter-state sale/purchase tax as a Union List subject, restricted state power over it
Abolished Part A/B/C/D state classification, reorganised states into 14 states and 6 union territories, extended HC jurisdiction to UTs
Extended SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation in Lok Sabha and assemblies by ten years, up to 1970
Facilitated cession of Berubari Union territory to Pakistan under the Indo-Pakistan Agreement
Incorporated Dadra and Nagar Haveli into the Indian Union
Changed Vice-President election procedure to an electoral college, protected election from vacancy-based challenge
Incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu into the Indian Union
Gave Nagaland statehood with special provisions
Incorporated Puducherry into the Indian Union, created legislatures and councils of ministers for certain union territories
Enabled high courts to issue writs beyond territorial jurisdiction, raised HC judges' retirement age to 62
Empowered restrictions on speech, assembly and association in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India
Required market-value compensation for acquisition of land under personal cultivation, added 44 more Acts to Ninth Schedule
Clarified Parliament's power to form new states includes forming them by uniting parts of states or union territories
Abolished Election Tribunals, vested power to hear election petitions in High Courts
Validated certain district judge appointments in Uttar Pradesh declared void by the Supreme Court
Included Sindhi as the 15th language in the Eighth Schedule
Facilitated creation of a new autonomous state of Meghalaya within Assam
Extended SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation for a further ten years, up to 1980
Affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights, made Presidential assent to amendment bills compulsory
Curtailed the fundamental right to property, protected laws implementing Article 39(b)/(c) from challenge under Articles 14, 19, 31
Abolished privy purses and privileges of former princely rulers
Empowered UT administrators to promulgate ordinances, made provisions for Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Manipur
Abolished special privileges of ICS officers, empowered Parliament to determine their service conditions
Included two Kerala land reform Acts in the Ninth Schedule
Removed the fixed monetary threshold for Supreme Court civil appeals, allowed appeal only on a substantial question of law
Increased the number of Lok Sabha seats from 525 to 545
Made special provisions to satisfy the aspirations of the Telangana region in Andhra Pradesh
Provided resignation of MPs/MLAs may only be accepted by Speaker/Chairman if satisfied it is voluntary and genuine
Included twenty more land tenure and land reform Acts of various states in the Ninth Schedule
Terminated Sikkim's protectorate status, conferred associate-state status via a new Tenth Schedule
Made Sikkim a full-fledged State of the Indian Union, omitted the Tenth Schedule
Provided legislative assembly and council of ministers for the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh
Made declaration of emergency and promulgation of ordinances non-justiciable, allowed multiple simultaneous emergency grounds
Placed election disputes of President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial scope
Empowered Parliament to specify limits of territorial waters, continental shelf and EEZ; added more laws to Ninth Schedule
Raised retirement age of State Public Service Commission and Joint Public Service Commission members from 60 to 62

Comprehensive 'Mini-Constitution' amendment: added socialist/secular/integrity to Preamble, added Fundamental Duties, curtailed judicial review, raised Lok Sabha/assembly tenure to 6 years, shifted subjects to Concurrent List, bound President by cabinet advice
Restored Supreme Court and High Court jurisdiction over judicial review and writs, removed Parliament's special anti-national-activity lawmaking powers
Restored 5-year Lok Sabha/assembly term and quorum requirements, deleted right to property from Fundamental Rights, protected Articles 20/21 during national emergency
Extended SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation for a further ten years, up to 1990
Enabled states to plug sales tax loopholes and bring uniformity to tax rates on certain items
Included 14 more land reform Acts of various states in the Ninth Schedule
Facilitated extension of President's rule in Punjab beyond one year without meeting the usual special conditions
Gave constitutional sanctity to the Autonomous District Council in Tripura
Empowered Parliament to restrict Fundamental Rights of persons employed in intelligence and telecommunication organisations for the armed forces
Provided reservation of Lok Sabha and assembly seats for STs in Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Mizoram
Provided for disqualification of MPs/MLAs on grounds of defection, added the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law)
Made special provisions for Mizoram, fixed minimum Assembly strength at 40 members
Increased salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges, allowed future changes by ordinary law
Made special provisions for Arunachal Pradesh, fixed minimum Assembly strength at 30 members
Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at a minimum of 30 members
Reserved assembly seats for STs in Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland
Provided an authoritative Hindi-language text of the Constitution with equal legal sanctity
Facilitated extension of President's Rule in Punjab up to three years, allowed national emergency declaration on internal disturbance grounds in Punjab
Increased ceiling of professional tax from Rs. 250 to Rs. 2,500 per annum
Reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and state assembly elections
Extended SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation for a further ten years, up to 2000
Repealed the 59th Amendment's changes, bringing Punjab at par with other states on emergency provisions
Facilitated extension of President's rule in Punjab to a total of three years six months
Established a multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs, replacing the earlier Special Officer
Included 55 more land reform Acts of various states in the Ninth Schedule
Facilitated extension of President's rule in Punjab to a total of four years
Facilitated extension of President's rule in Punjab to a total of five years
Accorded special status to Delhi as the National Capital Territory, created a 70-member legislative assembly and 7-member council of ministers

Provided an alternative scheme of revenue devolution between the Centre and states based on Tenth Finance Commission recommendations
Ended the 50% ceiling on reservation for unfilled backlog vacancies carried to succeeding years
Allowed relaxed qualifying marks or evaluation standards for SC/ST candidates in promotion to public services
Exempted Arunachal Pradesh from panchayat SC reservation requirements, as it has no SC population
Extended the ban on Lok Sabha/assembly seat readjustment for another 25 years to 2026, based on 1991 census figures
Provided consequential seniority for SC/ST government servants promoted under reservation, effective from June 1995
Made elementary education a fundamental right under new Article 21A, revised Article 45 and added a new fundamental duty
Provided for delimitation of constituencies based on the 2001 census instead of the 1991 census used earlier
Made provision for service tax, levied by the Centre but collected and appropriated by both Centre and states
Bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate constitutional bodies
Maintained existing ST and non-ST representation in the Assam assembly from Bodoland Territorial Areas District
Capped Council of Ministers size at 15% of house strength, debarred defectors from holding public office, strengthened anti-defection law
Included Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali in the Eighth Schedule, raising scheduled languages to 22
Empowered states to make reservation provisions for backward classes/SC/ST in private educational institutions, excluding minority institutions
Freed Bihar from the requirement of a tribal welfare minister, extended the same exemption to Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
Extended SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation for a further ten years, up to 2020
Substituted 'Odia' for 'Oriya' as the language name in the Eighth Schedule
Gave constitutional status to co-operative societies, made the right to form them a fundamental right, added new Part IX-B
Made special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka, covering local cadres and fund allocation
Replaced the collegium system with the National Judicial Appointments Commission for judge appointments; later struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015
Gave effect to the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, exchanging enclaves across four states
Paved the way for the Goods and Services Tax (GST), conferring concurrent taxing powers on Parliament and state legislatures
Conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes
Empowered states to provide up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections in education and public employment
Extended SC/ST reservation to 2030, discontinued Anglo-Indian nomination to Lok Sabha and state assemblies
Restored states' power to prepare and maintain their own list of socially and educationally backward classes
Reserved one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly for 15 years from commencement
